title: Energy ETL — where do the Spark jobs run?
description: The same two PySpark jobs and SQL models, three places to run them. Preview a variant from the status bar: nothing is written or deployed. Record decision is what commits a choice.

decisions.title: Where do the Spark jobs run?

options.label: A — local Spark
options.summary: spark-submit on a laptop over the sample CSV: to develop and demo, not to run the daily load.
cons: No scheduler, no Unity Catalog: tables are local

options.label: B — Databricks jobs
options.summary: The current architecture: one Databricks job (bundle meter-energy) with two tasks, started by the Airflow DAG.
pros: Declared in databricks.yml, checked with databricks bundle validate
cons: A workspace and a job cluster to pay for

options.label: C — Fabric Spark job definitions
options.summary: The same jobs as Fabric Spark job definitions in a Fabric workspace, the tables in a OneLake lakehouse.
pros: Lakehouse, notebooks and Power BI in one workspace
cons: A capacity to buy; its Git folder does not exist yet

scenarios.title: A — local Spark
scenarios.description: Files present: the jobs run with spark-submit over the sample.

scenarios.title: C — Fabric
scenarios.description: No files yet: its repository is planned.
